newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian snaps up Brussels' Mobutu mansion.
newsitem.headline: Belgian snaps up Brussels' Mobutu mansion.

text.p: A Belgian businessman said on Thursday he was buying a mansion owned by Mobutu Sese Seko, former president of Zaire (now the Democratic Republic of the Congo), near central Brussels.
But businessman Stephan Jourdain said the 200 million Belgian franc ($5.5 million) deal was being held up by technicalities.
"The sale is not yet effective because Belgian diplomatic authorities in Rabat have refused to recognise the legality of the deed," Jourdain told Reuters.
"Two entries on the document must be corrected: in fact Mobutu does not live in Kinshasa and he is not president of the Zaire Republic."
A spokesman for the Belgian Foreign Ministry declined to comment on Belgian press reports linking the delay to back taxes of 100 to 150 millions Belgian francs owed by Mobutu to the Belgian state.
Jourdain said he and Mobutu signed the initial documents on the sale two weeks ago in Rabat, Morocco, where the ailing ex-president found refuge after being ousted.
Mobutu bought the manor house of Fond'Roy-Uccle, a sumptuous building surrounded by a green park of five hectares, in the 1970s but has not lived there for 10 years, Belgian media said.
Jourdain said five members of the ex-president's private guard were still on the property.
